question.text: Will plant-based meat and seafood reach 10% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales before 2031?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, for any year before 2031, plant-based meat and seafood’s dollar share in the United States is greater than or equal to 10.0% of total retail packaged meat dollar sales, as reported by the [Good Food Institute](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/) (GFI).
question.fine_print:
Note that this question resolves based on share of the total retail packaged meat market and not the total meat category.

If the resolution source should have material issues such as failing to update in a timely manner, then Metaculus may name an alternative [credible source](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), as long as it judges the methodology to be substantially equivalent.

*Given the Animal Futures Tournament timeframe, scores from this question will not be included in the tournament leaderboard. However participants are required to predict on at least two of the three long-term questions, as per the tournament rules.*

research:
# Research brief: plant-based meat and seafood share of US retail packaged meat

## 1. Resolution source
- Latest data, 2025 (SPINS, 52 weeks ending 2025-11-30): GFI says plant-based meat and seafood made up **1.4% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales**, or about 0.7% of the total meat category including random-weight meat. Sales were about $1.0 billion, down 10% in dollars and 11% in units. Conventional meat and seafood rose 5% in dollars and 1% in units. GFI warns that its methodology changed, so these figures should not be compared directly with earlier years. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)
- The GFI page has no 2026 data yet.
- One small inconsistency: the question background gives $1.04B for 2025, while the GFI page says "about $1.0 billion".

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The share is 1.4% against a 10.0% threshold, so it would need to grow about 7 times.
- The share has fallen every year since its peak, and through 2026 the category is still shrinking while conventional meat grows.
- Timing: GFI publishes each year's full data around spring of the following year. That means 2029 data, released around April 2030, is probably the last that can come out before the question resolves around 2031-01-01. 2030 data would likely not be published in time. This is my reading of GFI's past release schedule, not something GFI has stated.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 net revenue fell 8.1% to $64.5M, with volume down 10.9%. US retail revenue fell 13.2% to $24.8M. It guided Q4 revenue to $54-59M, below Q3. [Food Manufacturing](https://www.foodmanufacturing.com/operations/news/22977953/beyond-meat-reports-q3-loss-of-828-million); [The Poultry Site](https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/11/beyond-meats-q3-revenue-falls-8-1)
- 2026-10 (August 2026 data, Circana via 210 Analytics): refrigerated plant-based meat sales were $22.7M for the month, down 10.2% year over year. Frozen meat alternatives were $61.4M, down about 7.8%. Stores carried 10.4% fewer refrigerated items than a year earlier. [210 Analytics/Circana PDF](https://assets.noviams.com/novi-file-uploads/pbfa/resources-toolkits/August_2026_210Analytics_Circana_meat_alternatives.pdf)
- 2026 (exact period not stated): SPINS shows US plant-based meat and seafood retail sales still down about 8% year over year, with shrinking shelf space and private label driving the decline. [The Plant Base](https://www.theplantbasemag.com/news/from-imitation-to-innovation-what-sets-apart-a-successful-plant-based-meat-brand)
- 2026-05-19: An industry analysis was titled "Why Plant-Based Meat's 'Future' Never Arrived". [Food Trade News](https://foodtradenews.com/2026/05/19/why-plant-based-meats-future-never-arrived/)
- Spring 2026: GFI's State of the Industry report found total US plant-based food sales down 2% to $7.9B, the second straight annual fall. Plant-based meat was the weakest segment. Shreds, chunks and strips grew 8% in units. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-globally); [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/)
- The 2026-11-10 news item about Logika Moloka covers Russian plant-based dairy and is not relevant to US meat share.

## 4. Base rates and trend
GFI's reported share of retail packaged meat dollar sales, by year:
- 2019: about 2%. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2021/04/06/2020-was-a-breakout-year-for-plant-based-foods-GFI-PBFA-SPINS-unveil-2020-retail-sales-data/)
- 2020: about 2.7%, the pandemic peak, when sales grew 46%. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2021/04/06/2020-was-a-breakout-year-for-plant-based-foods-GFI-PBFA-SPINS-unveil-2020-retail-sales-data/)
- 2021: about 2.7% (1.4% of total meat). [GFI press](https://gfi.org/press/u-s-plant-based-food-retail-sales-hit-7-4-billion/)
- 2022 and 2023: I could not find a confirmed figure.
- 2024: 1.7% under the earlier methodology. [search summary of GFI data](https://www.foodbusinessnews.net/articles/30327-plant-based-sales-in-the-us-continue-to-slide)
- 2025: 1.4%. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)

What this implies:
- The share has never reached 3%, let alone 10%.
- The best year on record (2020: +46% plant-based sales) raised the share by only about 0.7 points.
- Since 2022, plant-based dollar sales have changed by roughly -7% to -12% a year while conventional meat sales grew (+5% in 2025), so the share has been falling about 0.2-0.3 points a year.
- To reach 10% by 2029 from 1.4% in 2025, the share would need to grow about 60% a year, compounded, for four straight years. If conventional meat stays flat, that means plant-based sales of roughly $7B or more. No US year has come close.
- For comparison, GFI Europe has put plant-based meat at about 6% of pre-packaged meat in Europe in 2022, using different data and methods. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2023/04/11/is-there-any-evidence-the-plant-based-sector-can-move-from-niche-to-mainstream)

## 5. Other forecasts
- The market prices supplied with the question (US retail sales, LLMs, copper, EV share, AI market share, Dollar General, USD/CAD) are about other topics. None match this question.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on plant-based meat's share of US meat sales.
- Older optimistic industry projections exist, such as 2020-21 bank reports forecasting fast alt-protein growth. They came before the post-2021 decline and I did not verify them here.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around April 2027: GFI State of the Industry report and page update with 2026 SPINS data. Year-to-date signals point to another decline of roughly 8-10%. Similar releases should follow around spring 2028, 2029 and 2030.
- Late February or March 2027: Beyond Meat's Q4 and full-year 2026 results. Impossible Foods and private-label trends also matter, as do retailers cutting shelf space (down 10.4% year over year in August 2026).
- Possible game-changers I found no evidence of: price parity with animal meat, a big jump in conventional meat prices, regulatory shocks, or GFI changing its methodology or how it defines the denominator. Any of these could move the share faster than the trend.
- Cultivated meat probably does not count toward this measure, which covers plant-based products only.

I found nothing that has already settled this. By GFI's own figures, plant-based meat and seafood is far below the 10.0% threshold and still falling: it was 1.4% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales in 2025. Only the 2026, 2027, 2028 and 2029 figures can count, plus 2030 if GFI publishes it before the question closes. To reach 10%, the share would have to rise roughly 7-fold from where it is now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026 (page undated, copyright 2026, data through November 30, 2025): GFI's resolution page reports US plant-based meat and seafood at about $1.0B in 2025, down 10% in dollars and 11% in units. It was **1.4% of total retail packaged meat dollar sales**, or about 0.7% of the total meat category including random-weight meat. The data come from SPINS, covering MULO, Natural Expanded and Convenience channels, with Circana supplying the MULO and Convenience data. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)
- 2026-05: The full figures are in GFI's 2026 State of the Industry report. Searches of GFI's market overview say the 2025 share was down 0.24 percentage points from 2024. [GFI SOTI PDF](https://gfi.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GFI_2026-State-of-the-Industry-Plant-based-meat-seafood-eggs-dairy-and-ingredients.pdf), [GFI market research](https://gfi.org/marketresearch/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The latest value, 1.4% for 2025, is about one-seventh of the threshold, and the share has fallen every year since 2021.
- In the natural channel alone, the share was higher: 8% in 2024, and about 15% in an earlier year (likely 2023) by one report. These channel figures are not the resolution metric. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-globally), [GFI 2023 outlook](https://gfi.org/blog/2023-outlook-the-state-of-the-plant-based-meat-category/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-05: Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 revenue was $64.5M, down 8.1%, its seventh straight quarterly decline. US retail fell 13.2% to $24.8M, with volume down 20.8%. The CEO cited "weak category demand," inflation and doubts about how healthy the products are. Guidance implies full-year 2026 sales down about 9%. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/?p=89722)
- 2026-05-07: Beyond Meat's Q1 2026 revenue fell 15.3%, after a 19.7% drop in Q4 2025. [FoodNavigator-USA](https://www.foodnavigator-usa.com/Article/2026/05/07/beyond-meat-q1-2026-results/)
- 2026 (spring): GFI's 2026 report says total US plant-based food sales fell 2% to $7.9B in 2025, and only 11% of households bought plant-based meat or seafood. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/), [Cultivated X](https://cultivated-x.com/studies-numbers/gfis-2026-state-of-industry-reports-detail-mixed-year-alternative-proteins-across-three-sectors/)
- Circana data show refrigerated plant-based meat "in freefall," with frozen starting to level off. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-us-retail-refrigerated-remains-in-freefall-frozen-starting-to-plateau)
- I could not find any 2026 year-to-date SPINS or GFI category figures.

## 4. Base rates
GFI's share of retail packaged meat dollar sales, by year:
- 2020: 2.7%. [FoodNavigator-USA](https://www.foodnavigator-usa.com/Article/2021/04/06/2020-was-a-breakout-year-for-plant-based-foods-GFI-PBFA-SPINS-unveil-2020-retail-sales-data)
- 2021: 2.7%, or 1.4% of total meat. [GFI 2021 PDF](https://gfi.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/2021-U.S.-retail-market-insights_Plant-based-foods-GFI.pdf)
- 2022: 2.5%, or 1.3% of total meat. [GFI](https://gfi.org/blog/2023-outlook-the-state-of-the-plant-based-meat-category/)
- 2023: I could not confirm a packaged-meat figure.
- 2024: 1.7%, or about 0.8% of total meat. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-globally)
- 2025: 1.4%. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)

What the history shows:
- The share has never been higher than about 2.7%.
- The biggest single-year jump came in the 2020 pandemic year, when sales grew 46%. Even then the share rose by well under one percentage point, given that 2019 sales were $957M.
- Since 2021 the share has fallen by about 0.2 to 0.3 points a year.
- For a rough sense of scale: holding conventional packaged meat sales flat, reaching 10% would take plant-based sales of roughly $7.4B, about 7 times the 2025 level, within 4 to 5 years. That works out to around 50% or more growth every year. If meat prices keep rising, the denominator grows and the target gets harder.
- No national market comes close. Europe-wide, the share of pre-packaged meat was 6% in 2022 and the UK's was 3%. [GFI Europe](https://gfieurope.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/2020-2022-Europe-retail-market-insights.pdf)

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prices collected by code match this question. They cover retail sales overall, EV share, LLMs and similar topics.
- Manifold has a market asking whether "fake meat" will reach 10% or more of the US meat market by 2035. A search snippet showed it at 73%. I could not check this, and it looks out of line with the data; it may also use a different metric. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Ivan/when-will-the-meat-substitute-marke)
- A Metaculus question on alternative proteins passing 25% share by 2035 shows about 4.5%, based on 82 forecasters. That figure is also from a search snippet and I did not check it. [GFI/Metaculus tournament](https://gfi.org/blog/alt-protein-tournament/)
- Metaculus also has a question on the value of the US plant-based meat market for the year ending April 2028. [Metaculus](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/3095/us-plant-based-meat-market-cap-april-2028)
- I found no expert forecast that puts US plant-based meat anywhere near 10% of packaged meat by 2030.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- GFI's 2026 State of the Industry figures, with full-year 2026 data, are expected around March to May 2027. Further releases should follow in spring 2028, 2029 and 2030. A 2030 figure would come out after the question closes on 2030-12-31.
- Beyond Meat's Q4 and full-year 2026 results, due around February to March 2027, will be an early signal.
- Possible upside factors are big changes in price or taste, such as reaching price parity or new whole-cut or mycelium products. Changes in conventional meat prices or supply, for example beef prices or bird flu, would also move the share by changing the denominator.
- Other risks: GFI could change its methodology or channels, for example in SPINS coverage, or stop updating. In that case Metaculus may pick another source.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires:** About 4 years remain. In practice, only GFI's 2026, 2027, 2028 and 2029 figures, released roughly each spring from 2027 to 2030, can arrive before close. 2030 data would likely be published after 2030-12-31. Yes requires GFI to report plant-based meat and seafood at 10.0% or more of US retail packaged meat dollar sales for one of those years.

**(b) Status quo:** The share was 1.4% in 2025 and has fallen about 0.2-0.3 points a year since 2021. 2026 data so far show plant-based sales down a further 8-10% while conventional meat grows. The status quo outcome is No.

**(c) Base rate:** Mature food categories almost never grow their market share 7-fold in 4 years from a declining position. US plant-based meat peaked at about 2.7% even in its best year, 2020, when sales grew 46% and the share rose under 1 point. Europe, the strongest region, reached only about 6%. Base rate: well under 1%.

**(d) Evidence:**
- **For Yes (weak):**
  - Whole-cut and shred formats grew 8% in units (spring 2026 report).
  - Health positioning is producing some winning products.
  - Natural-channel shares are high, but that channel is not the resolution metric.
- **For No (strong):**
  - The share was 1.4% in 2025 (GFI, data through November 2025).
  - Beyond Meat's US retail revenue fell 13.2% in Q3 2026 (reported November 2026).
  - Circana's August 2026 data show refrigerated plant-based meat down 10.2%, with 10.4% fewer items on shelves.
  - Only 11% of households buy plant-based meat.
  - Conventional meat dollar sales are rising (+5% in 2025).

**(e) Scenarios:**
- **No:** The decline continues or flattens, and the share sits around 1-1.5% through 2029. This is near-certain.
- **Yes:** Requires something like a price-parity breakthrough plus a massive animal-meat supply shock, or a radical GFI change to the denominator definition. Even then, plant-based sales would need to exceed about $7B within 3 years, implausibly fast.

**(f) Adjustment:** No market covers this exact question. The unverified Manifold 73% figure uses a different metric and horizon, and appears unreliable. I start from a base rate under 1% and add a sliver for definitional or methodology surprises. The outcome cannot realistically change before the deadline given the size of the gap and the falling trend, so a sub-3% forecast is justified.

Probability: 1%

(a) About four years remain. Data for 2026 through 2029 should be released by spring 2030, and 2030 data likely won't appear before resolution. For Yes, GFI must report plant-based meat and seafood at 10.0% or more of US retail packaged meat dollar sales for some year before 2031.

(b) Status quo: the share was 1.4% in 2025 and is still falling about 0.2 to 0.3 points a year. 2026 data on sales, shelf space and Beyond Meat results all point to further decline. The status quo outcome is No.

(c) Base rate: established consumer food categories almost never grow their market share 7-fold in four years, especially after four straight years of decline. In those circumstances the base rate is well under 1%. The category's best year, 2020 with +46% sales, added only about 0.7 points of share.

(d) Evidence for Yes is weak:
- Whole-cut alternatives grew 8% in units in 2025, and products with health claims gained in 2025 to 2026.
- The natural channel share was about 8% in 2024, but that is not the resolution metric.
- An unverified Manifold market reportedly sits at 73% for a "fake meat" 10% share by 2035. It likely uses a different metric and looks miscalibrated.

Evidence for No is strong:
- GFI reported the 2025 share at 1.4%, down 0.24 points.
- Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 US retail revenue fell 13.2% (reported 2026-11-04/05).
- Circana data for August 2026 show refrigerated sales down 10.2% and refrigerated item counts down 10.4%.
- SPINS shows 2026 sales down about 8%.
- Conventional meat sales are growing, so the denominator is rising.

(e) No scenario: the decline continues or levels off around 1 to 1.5%, and every GFI release through 2030 shows under 2%.

Yes scenario: a breakthrough product reaches price and taste parity, combined with a severe meat supply shock such as bird flu or beef shortages. Plant-based sales would then need to grow about 60% a year through 2029. Alternatively, GFI could redefine the denominator to something far narrower and Metaculus could accept it. Both paths are extremely unlikely.

(f) I start below 1% and add a little for tail risks: methodology or denominator changes, or an unforeseen technology or supply shock. With four or more years of uncertainty, I stay just above the floor rather than at it.

Probability: 1%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires**
Only GFI-reported annual figures for 2026 through 2029 can realistically count. 2030 data would likely be published around spring 2031, after the question closes. Yes requires plant-based meat and seafood to reach at least 10.0% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales in one of those years. The first new data point, for 2026, arrives around spring 2027 and the last around spring 2030.

**(b) Status quo**
The share was 1.4% in 2025 and has fallen every year since 2021. Category sales are still declining about 8-10% in 2026 while conventional meat grows. If nothing changes, the answer is clearly No.

**(c) Base rate**
I found no case of a US food-substitute category raising its share roughly 7-fold in 3-4 years from a declining base. The record US year for this category was 2020, with 46% sales growth, and it added only about 0.7 points of share. The highest share ever recorded is about 2.7%. Even Europe, the strongest region, was at about 6% in 2022. The base rate is well under 1%.

**(d) Evidence**
- **For Yes (weak):**
  - Whole-cut and shreds products grew 8% in units (GFI, spring 2026).
  - Products with health positioning are seeing some growth.
  - A methodology or denominator change by GFI is possible.
- **For No (strong):**
  - GFI reports a 1.4% share for 2025, down 0.24 points from 2024.
  - SPINS shows 2026 sales down about 8%.
